introduction: A broad, varied area south of Market, where older commercial buildings, restored landmarks and larger offices sit alongside housing and cultural uses. The individual block matters as much as the district name.
character: The Central SoMa plan documents an industrial legacy and an evolving employment and residential neighborhood. Its defined planning area is only part of SoMa; do not apply its boundaries or policies to the whole district.
soma.fit: Worth comparing when you want several office formats in one search, from a restored landmark to a larger modern workplace. Start with the commute and daily walk from each address, then compare layout and building access.
soma.check: Compare the actual walk from transit, building access, layout and fit-out condition. The Central SoMa planning area covers only part of SoMa; its policies do not apply uniformly across this wider guide.
soma.geography: Compare individual addresses and nearby areas. Shading and plotted examples are approximate locations, not legal boundaries or a list of available spaces.

introduction: A planned mixed-use neighborhood shaped by UCSF, medical care, research buildings, offices, housing and parks.
mission-bay.characterHeading: A neighborhood shaped by research and redevelopment
character: OCII documents the transformation of former Southern Pacific rail yards and surrounding land, with redevelopment plans approved in 1998. Mission Bay South includes the UCSF campus and medical center, Chase Center, and office and biotech uses.
mission-bay.fit: Worth exploring when regular work brings you close to UCSF, health care or research activity. Compare the exact office or lab requirements separately; nearby institutions do not make a building lab-ready.
mission-bay.check: Separate office and laboratory requirements, including permitted use and technical infrastructure. Check actual travel routes and event-day access. A nearby institution does not make a commercial building lab-ready.
mission-bay.geography: Compare individual addresses and nearby areas. Shading and plotted examples are approximate locations, not legal boundaries or a list of available spaces.

introduction: A mixed-use waterfront setting combining office buildings, housing, parks and older commercial landmarks.
south-beach.characterHeading: An evolving waterfront, with several kinds of workplace
character: OCII describes the Rincon Point–South Beach redevelopment, begun in 1981, as a mix of rehabilitation and new development. Its commercial projects include Rincon Center, alongside waterfront parks and housing.
south-beach.fit: Worth comparing if you want an office near the Embarcadero and value a waterfront walk as part of the working day. Compare the northern office blocks and southern waterfront addresses individually.
south-beach.check: Check the entrance, the route from your relevant station and the particular suite. A waterfront-area address does not guarantee a water view. District names overlap in marketing, so compare addresses rather than assume one universal boundary.
south-beach.geography: Compare individual addresses and nearby areas. Shading and plotted examples are approximate locations, not legal boundaries or a list of available spaces.

introduction: An industrial waterfront neighborhood with historic factory buildings, maker and production activity, and continuing redevelopment.
dogpatch.characterHeading: Industrial heritage on a changing waterfront
character: The city's Central Waterfront planning framework and Dogpatch public-realm plan describe industrial heritage alongside a changing mixed-use waterfront. Approved Power Station proposals are future development context, not proof that buildings are delivered or available.
dogpatch.fit: Worth exploring when the work itself needs a practical industrial or creative setting. Start with permitted use, loading, power, ventilation and employee access rather than assuming an attractive conversion can support the operation.
dogpatch.check: Confirm permitted use, loading, power, ventilation and employee access. Industrial character is not a technical specification. Separate an existing building from approved future development.
dogpatch.geography: Compare individual addresses and nearby areas. Shading and plotted examples are approximate locations, not legal boundaries or a list of available spaces.

introduction: A residential hill neighborhood with commercial and production-oriented edges. A hilltop address and a lower industrial block can offer very different working-day experiences.
potrero-hill.characterHeading: The hill and its commercial edges
character: The Showplace Square/Potrero plan records the area's warehouse and industrial history and continuing role for production, distribution and repair. That combined planning area includes Showplace Square, so its furniture-design history should not be attributed uniformly to all of Potrero Hill.
potrero-hill.fit: Worth exploring for a neighborhood workplace or a business that benefits from nearby production and maker activity. Compare slope, the final walk to transit, loading and visitor access at the exact address.
potrero-hill.check: Compare the slope, final walk, loading and visitor access at the exact address. Views, parking and step-free arrival vary. A production workspace and a conventional office need different checks.
potrero-hill.geography: Compare individual addresses and nearby areas. Shading and plotted examples are approximate locations, not legal boundaries or a list of available spaces.

introduction: A neighborhood of local shops, food, cultural activity and production spaces, with a strong Latino cultural identity and a mix of everyday commercial uses.
character: The Mission Area Plan documents retail corridors alongside northeast Mission production, distribution and repair activity. Its population and employment figures are historical planning context and are not reused as current statistics.
mission-district.fit: Worth exploring for a neighborhood-facing business or a creative or production team that values being part of an active local setting. Compare the corridor, noise, deliveries and customer access before focusing on the building alone.
mission-district.check: Compare the corridor, noise, deliveries and customer access. Confirm permitted use, accessibility and acoustic privacy. Neighborhood character alone cannot establish operational suitability.
mission-district.geography: Compare individual addresses and nearby areas. Shading and plotted examples are approximate locations, not legal boundaries or a list of available spaces.
